title: Affliction Is a Stormy Deep
description: Affliction Is a Stormy Deep in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Nathaniel Cotton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 609 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God, the Refuge of the Afflicted”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: A-fflic-tion is a storm-y deep, Where wave re-sounds to wave; Though o'er our heads the bil-lows roll, We know the Lord can save.

lines: Though o'er our heads the billows roll,
We know the Lord can save.
When darkness and when sorrows rose,
The Lord hath still sustained our steps,
And still hath been our Guide.
For he who bade the tempest roar,
Here will we rest, here build our hopes,
He's more to us than all the world,
Our Health, our Life, our God.

licence: Public domain: Nathaniel Cotton died in 1788.
credits: Words by Nathaniel Cotton (1705–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
